suggestions.title: Book the DEXA. The scale can't answer this week's question and a scan answers it in one morning.

rationale.science: At a rate near zero the scale tells you nothing about the fat/lean split. The protective range on a cut is 0.5-0.7% of bodyweight a week (Garthe 2011); you're at 0.04%, so the question isn't whether you're losing too fast — it's what the flat number is made of, and only a body-composition measurement answers that.
rationale.data: Trend 163.6 to 164.07 over a fortnight on a logged mean of 2,263 calories against measured maintenance of 2,634-2,708. Over the same days, in one session on 8/14: hack 180 to 200 (7,7,8), extension 155 to 160 (8,9), ham 120 to 125 (11,9,9), abs 100 x 14,14,14. Protein averaging 180 g, eleven weeks at 100%.
rationale.relationship: A food log that's short by ~400 a day and a genuine recomp produce the identical flat scale and mean opposite things about your fat. Rising loads point at recomp — but loads rise on a mis-counted diet too. q_dexa has sat UNBOOKED since it was queued: Jericho NY, fasted, normal day, two days clear of a refeed.

suggestions.predict: The scan re-anchors the body-fat model and decides which of the two explanations I've been arguing with myself about is right. I'm not predicting the scale — I'm saying the scale can't settle this and I've spent a week proving it.

suggestions.title: For seven days, log anything you didn't cook yourself on the day you eat it.

rationale.science: When a rate stalls, logging drift and portion creep explain it far more often than metabolism. Metabolic adaptation is real but modest, roughly 50-100 calories a day for moderate loss, and it fades (Alhassan 2008; Nunes 2021).
rationale.data: 8/9-8/13 logged 2,350 / 2,231 / 2,279 / 2,249 / 2,208 (mean 2,263) on 14,700-19,500 steps. Against maintenance of 2,634 (my fit) or 2,708 (your app's) that's a stated 370-445 calorie deficit, which should read 0.75-0.9 lb a week down. The trend went up 0.3 lb instead. The gap is 400-475 calories a day. Sodium is blank on 8/9, 8/10, 8/12 and 8/13 — four of those six days.
rationale.relationship: The blank sodium days are the days you ate something you didn't make, and those are exactly the days a calorie count is a guess rather than a measurement. Same-day logging is the only one of the two explanations for this stall that you can test this week — and it costs nothing if the log is already right.

suggestions.predict: If the log is accurate as written, seven same-day days change the mean by less than 100 and the trend reads at or under 163.4 by Saturday 8/22 — which puts the error on my maintenance estimate instead, and I'll say so. If the logged mean rises 200 or more, the gap was bookkeeping and neither of us knew the real deficit.

suggestions.title: Press tomorrow: run three honest sets, or make the fourth one honest. Your best press scored nothing.

rationale.science: On a cut, defend load rather than chase volume, and take working sets to about 1-3 reps in reserve (Schoenfeld 2017; Robinson 2024).
rationale.data: On 8/9 press ran 250 x 8,8,7,4 — the best press in your file — and drew no feed row at all, while rows, tricep, sulek and lateral each drew one from the same session. Press is still on file at 4 sets at 250, unchanged since.
rationale.relationship: My read is that the fourth set adds a fourth target the short set fails, which sinks the whole lift's score no matter how good the first three were. That is a best guess, not a measurement — the target array isn't saved, so I can't check it. Tomorrow matters because it's your first upper day in a week, no volume push lands until Monday, and press is one of the few lifts Monday's two new exercises do NOT re-baseline.

suggestions.predict: Three sets at 250 x 8,8,7 draws a press row. Four sets with a short fourth draws nothing again. If four sets with a short fourth does draw a row, my reading of the scoring is wrong and I withdraw it.
